Early morning overcast skies and surface temperatures near 62°F at DFW International Airport create uncertainty in afternoon insolation and heating rates, with model ensembles like GFS showing tight clustering around 76-79°F. Monitor hourly NWS guidance and real-time DFW observations for intraday shifts toward resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: India Meteorological Department observations at Chaudhary Charan Singh International Airport confirm Lucknow's maximum temperature reached 36.3°C on May 11, 2026—3.5°C below seasonal norms—driving trader consensus to 100% implied probability for "36°C or below," as this aligns with the market's lowest bin based on official airport readings. Persistent cloud cover and cooler air masses from Uttar Pradesh's 730% above-normal early May rainfall, including the second-coolest May day in 57 years at 28°C on May 5, have capped pre-monsoon heat well below the typical 40°C+ highs. IMD forecast models anticipated this 36°C peak under clear skies, with no intensification signals. Realistic challenges would require a late revision to airport data exceeding 36.9°C or discrepancies in final bulletins, though precedents favor observed values locking resolution soon.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket has locked in 23°C as the highest temperature at Warsaw Chopin Airport today with near-certainty, driven by the latest forecasts from Poland's Institute of Meteorology and Water Management (IMGW), AccuWeather, and ensemble models like ECMWF and GFS, which project peak midday heating under a temporary high-pressure ridge before an advancing frontal boundary brings cloud cover, showers, and possible thunderstorms. Current observations confirm this positioning, with airport readings reaching 22–23°C (72–73°F) around 2 p.m. amid initial sunshine, now transitioning to overcast skies limiting further insolation. Realistic challenges include delayed cloud onset allowing extra solar warming to 24°C or cooler northerly winds suppressing the peak, though model agreement and real-time data strongly favor resolution at 23°C; monitor IMGW hourly updates and official station records through evening.

Current observations show haze with temperatures in the low 60s°F and 80% humidity at LAX, aligning with an overnight low near 58°F and onshore winds limiting solar insolation despite typical May Gray patterns. This reflects a week of similar cool anomalies from cool Pacific sea surface temperatures, matching LAX's climatological normal high of 69°F. Faster afternoon clearing could push toward 70-71°F (29% odds), with final resolution from Weather Underground data later today.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket has locked in 100% implied probability for Istanbul's highest temperature reaching 25°C or higher on May 11, driven by real-time observational data from the Turkish State Meteorological Service (MGM) and airport stations showing mid-afternoon readings already at 25-26°C under hazy sunshine and light winds. High-pressure ridging over the eastern Mediterranean has suppressed clouds, enabling rapid daytime heating above the May historical average of 22°C, with model consensus from ECMWF and GFS projecting peaks near 27°C before sunset. Final resolution awaits NOAA-verified highs at Istanbul Airport (LTFM) by midnight local time. Realistic challenges are minimal—only an unforeseen strong sea breeze or convective downdraft could cap temperatures below 25°C, but current trajectories and short remaining daylight render this improbable.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket reflects tight uncertainty in National Weather Service forecasts for San Francisco's May 12 high temperature, with models clustering around 62–66°F due to persistent marine stratus from cool Pacific sea surface temperatures near 55°F and west-southwest winds of 10–20 mph limiting coastal warming. Recent NWS updates show partial afternoon clearing after overnight lows near 52–53°F, boosting the 66°F or higher implied probability to 33.5% as some guidance like GFS hints at earlier burn-off and subsidence from a building high-pressure ridge; however, ECMWF leans cooler with prolonged clouds favoring 62–65°F outcomes. Key differentiator is boundary layer mixing—stronger onshore flow caps peaks at 62–63°F (27%), while lighter winds enable 64–65°F (28.5%). Watch this afternoon's forecast discussion from the NWS San Francisco Bay Area office for model shifts ahead of peak heating around 2–4 p.m.

Differentiating factors include thunderstorm onset timing: early development caps highs at 32-33°C via shading and downdrafts, while delays allow 34°C; high humidity near 80% and urban heat island effects add variability. eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket reflects deep uncertainty for Wuhan's May 13 highest temperature, with 41% implied probabilities for 20°C or below and 30°C or higher amid forecasts centering 28–29°C from AccuWeather and BBC Weather. This split stems from ensemble model disagreements on cloud cover and light precipitation timing—drizzle or thundery showers per BBC could cap daytime heating below 21°C via increased humidity and northerly wind shifts (NW 5 mph AccuWeather), while southerly flows and partial clearing favor 30°C+ persistence. Recent observations show warming (May 10 high 28°C, May 11 forecast 30–31°C sunny), but short-range China Meteorological Administration updates and ECMWF/GFS runs due within 24 hours may resolve the bimodal outlook against May climatological norms of 26–28°C highs.
